rejected.title: Choosing devices for an effect
card: In your own writing, start with the effect you want the reader to feel. Then pick a device that suits it.
Suspense
Use short sentences to build suspense. Example: A shadow moved. I stopped. Waited.
Humour
Use exaggeration to make a reader smile. Example: My brother's snore was so loud that the neighbours' dog filed a complaint.
A device that does not suit the effect can weaken the writing. A grim, serious tone could flatten a funny story, and long, drifting sentences could slow a chase scene.
rejected.remember: Decide the effect first, then choose the device that will create it.

a.q: Lena is writing a funny story about a messy bedroom. Which device suits her aim best?
opts: Exaggeration, such as a sock pile as tall as a tree
Short sentences, such as: A creak. Silence. A step
Long, drifting sentences, such as a slow slide into sleep
A grim, serious tone, such as a sad report on the mess
a.why: Exaggeration makes a reader smile because the claim is clearly too big to be true. Short sentences suit a tense scene, not a funny one, and a grim tone could flatten the humour.
a.clue: Which device is used to get a laugh?

b.q: Tom is writing a scene where a girl hears something behind her in an empty school. He wants the reader to feel on edge. Which choice is best?
opts: Short sentences, such as: A noise. Closer. She froze
One long sentence about the peaceful, sunlit corridor
Exaggeration, such as a cough that shook the whole town
A silly joke, such as the noise being a dancing mop
b.why: Short, sharp sentences build tension, which suits the effect of suspense. Exaggeration is tempting because it is a strong device, but the card links it to humour, and a comic image could spoil the tense mood.
b.clue: Match the device to the feeling of being on edge.
